c.tagline: Thundering falls, neon-lit Clifton Hill, and Niagara wine country right next door
langs: French (official Canadian second language, limited local use)

card: Widely accepted everywhere, including tap-to-pay; cash mainly useful for small vendors

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly CAD $3.25 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Rides between Clifton Hill and Fallsview hotels are short; agree a flat rate for trips to the wine region

emergency.note: 911 reaches police, fire, and ambulance across Canada

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Central Fallsview and Clifton Hill are very walkable along the Falls; reaching Niagara-on-the-Lake wineries or Chippawa requires a car, bus, or WEGO shuttle

safety.safety: Very safe, well-patrolled tourist zone with heavy foot traffic day and night
safety.crime: Petty tourist scams and overpriced attractions are the main risk, not violent crime

hood_landmark.Clifton Hill: Clifton Hill's neon arcades and haunted houses
hood_landmark.Fallsview: Niagara Fallsview Casino Resort overlooking the Horseshoe Falls
hood_landmark.Queen Street (Downtown): Queen Street's emerging arts and antiques district
hood_landmark.Chippawa: Historic Chippawa village on the upper Niagara River
hood_landmark.Niagara Parkway / Dufferin Islands: Dufferin Islands Nature Area along the scenic parkway

avoid.reason: Clifton Hill's tourist strip has inflated prices and occasional aggressive touts; watch belongings in peak-season crowds.

hood_desc: The carnival-bright entertainment strip of arcades, wax museums, and mini-golf a short walk from the Falls; suits families and first-time visitors wanting everything within stumbling distance.
The high-rise hotel and casino district with the best direct Falls views from guest rooms and restaurants; suits travelers prioritizing the view over budget.
A quieter revitalizing downtown with antique shops, cafes, and the VIA Rail station, a short drive or bus ride from the Falls themselves.
A historic riverside village upstream from the Falls with War of 1812 heritage sites and a slower pace; suits those wanting to escape the tourist crowds.
A green, walkable stretch of parkland and gardens along the upper river, good for cycling and a break from the casino strip.
lodging: Four Points by Sheraton Niagara Falls
The Oakes Hotel Overlooking the Falls

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.sys: WEGO shuttle buses linking hotels, attractions, and the Falls; Niagara Region Transit for wider area
transit.hours: WEGO runs roughly 9am-11pm (extended in peak summer)
transit.pay: Cash or tap card on WEGO buses; day passes available
transit.note: The Falls area itself is very walkable; a car is useful for wine country or Niagara-on-the-Lake

transport.air: Toronto Pearson International (YYZ), about 1.5 hr; Buffalo Niagara International (BUF, USA) is closer at 25-30 min
transport.train: VIA Rail station with service to Toronto and connections onward
transport.bus: GO Transit and Megabus connect to Toronto and other Ontario cities
transport.car: Easy via the QEW highway from Toronto; parking at Falls-area lots and garages

airport.name: Toronto Pearson International Airport
airport.transport: Airport shuttles, GO Transit/bus combinations, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Canadian prepaid SIM or eSIM from Rogers/Bell/Telus

tip.s: 10-15% is standard for tours and guided experiences
tip.r: 15-18% is expected at restaurants; often added automatically for larger groups
